tooltip.title: Treatment of Androgenetic Alopecia
tooltip.markdown: A step-wise approach focusing on stimulating growth, blocking androgens, and procedural enhancement.

tooltip.title: Minoxidil for AGA
tooltip.markdown: Topical minoxidil is an established option; strength and application schedule depend on the product and population. Low-dose oral minoxidil is off-label for alopecia and requires individualized cardiovascular, renal, pregnancy, and interaction assessment. In a 24-week randomized trial in men, oral 5 mg daily did not demonstrate superiority over topical 5% twice daily for the primary hair-density outcomes.

tooltip.title: 5-alpha Reductase Inhibitors
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Finasteride (1mg):** FDA-approved for male AGA.
-   **Dutasteride (0.5mg):** Off-label but more potent than finasteride.
-   **Use in Women:** Can be used off-label in postmenopausal women or those on reliable contraception.

tooltip.title: Therapies Primarily for Female Pattern Hair Loss
Spironolactone
tooltip.markdown: An oral anti-androgen used off-label for FPHL. Doses typically range from 50-200 mg daily.

tooltip.title: Procedural Interventions for AGA
tooltip.markdown: In-office treatments to supplement medical therapy.

tooltip.title: PRP for AGA
tooltip.markdown: Used to increase hair count and density. A typical regimen is monthly injections for 3 months, followed by maintenance.

tooltip.title: LLLT for AGA
tooltip.markdown: At-home devices (caps, helmets) used several times per week to stimulate growth. Best for those with mild-to-moderate AGA.

tooltip.title: Surgical Options for AGA
tooltip.markdown: Hair transplantation redistributes donor follicles in selected candidates. It is not the only possible route to visible regrowth where viable miniaturized follicles remain; medical treatment and realistic donor-area assessment remain important.

tooltip.title: Hair Transplantation
tooltip.markdown: An excellent option for suitable candidates with sufficient donor hair and realistic expectations. Medical therapy is crucial to maintain non-transplanted hair.
